Entropy-Based Ranking Measure

Source: R/centrality-batch68.R
centrality_erm.Rd

The entropy-based ranking measure (ERM; Zareie et al. 2017) gives each node an entropy centrality from the spread of its neighbors' degrees and of their degree sums, and adds it over the walks of two steps: $$ERM(i) = \sum_{j \in N(i)} \sum_{l \in N(j)} EC(l), \qquad EC(i) = E_1(i) + \lambda_i E_2(i), \qquad \lambda_i = \frac{k^{(2)}_i}{\max_l k^{(2)}_l},$$ with \(E_1(i)\) the entropy of the shares \(k_j / k^{(1)}_i\) over the neighbors \(j\) of \(i\), \(E_2(i)\) that of the shares \(k^{(1)}_j / k^{(2)}_i\), \(k\) the degree, \(k^{(1)}_i\) the sum of the neighbors' degrees and \(k^{(2)}_i\) the sum of the neighbors' \(k^{(1)}\).

Usage

centrality_erm(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Network input accepted by centrality.

...

Further arguments to centrality, such as normalized.

Value

A named numeric vector with one score per node, in input node order.

Details

The measure is computed on the simple undirected skeleton of the network, so direction, weights, loops and parallel edges are ignored. The source's equation (4) is printed with \(v_j\) on its right side; the sentence that introduces it, and the same authors' restatement (Zareie and Sheikhahmadi 2019, equation 9), have \(v_i\). The source gives no base for the logarithm; the natural logarithm is used (owner decision 2026-11-26), and another base multiplies every score by one constant. A leaf has \(EC = 0\); a node scores through the nodes its walks of two steps reach, so a leaf of a star scores 0, and so does an isolated node. The source prints no score. The implementation reproduces the share of distinct ranks and the monotonicity of its 21-node example (0.8095 and 0.9623) and of the dolphins network (0.9677 and 0.9979), and the monotonicity Zareie et al. (2020) print for the adjective-noun network (0.9997); each of these is also the largest value an exact structural measure can reach on its network, so they show only that the measure separates every pair of nodes the network does not make equivalent. On the karate club the source prints 0.8529 and 0.9612, above the largest values an exact structural measure can reach there (0.7941 and 0.9542, the values of the implementation). On four test networks the score ranks nodes closest to centrality_ninl (mean Kendall correlation 0.984) and centrality_diffusion_centrality (0.978); with centrality_eigenvector the correlation is 0.92 to 0.99. normalized = TRUE divides the scores by their maximum.

References

Zareie, A., Sheikhahmadi, A. and Fatemi, A. (2017). Influential nodes ranking in complex networks: an entropy-based approach. Chaos, Solitons and Fractals, 104, 485-494. doi:10.1016/j.chaos.2017.09.010 .

Zareie, A., Sheikhahmadi, A., Jalili, M. and Fasaei, M. S. K. (2020). Finding influential nodes in social networks based on neighborhood correlation coefficient. Knowledge-Based Systems, 194, 105580. doi:10.1016/j.knosys.2020.105580 .

See also

centrality_ehc, centrality_ecrm, centrality_entropy, centrality.

Examples

centrality_erm(regulation_net)
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>   82.41142  101.18502  114.72021   97.75951   81.09264   83.18577   70.38873 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>   88.83466  102.44021   89.38820
